hints.text: Take a tiny example, say a = [1, 4] and b = [2, 3]. Where in the code does the list get sorted each time an element is appended?

The evidence shows that any algorithm that only compares elements needs Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case. By calling sort() inside each loop iteration you are performing a comparison‑sort on a growing list many times, which contradicts the required O(|a|+|b|) work.

Recall the definition of O‑notation: it describes an upper bound on growth rate. What is the asymptotic cost of sorting k elements, and how does that cost multiplied by the number of loop iterations compare to O(|a|+|b|)?
